title: Cross-Boundary Vulnerability Management for SDVs: A Traceability Architecture at the ISO/SAE 21434 and EU Cyber Resilience Act Interface
abstract: arXiv:2611.28303v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: A software-defined vehicle depends on products that sit under different EU regimes. The type-approved vehicle and the systems, components and separate technical units made for it fall under Regulation (EU) 2019/2144, which makes UN R155 mandatory; Regulation (EU) 2018/858 does so for R156; and ISO/SAE 21434 supports the management system R155 requires. Chargers, companion apps, aftermarket devices and many backends may fall under the Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) instead, whose reporting duty in Article 14 has applied since 11 September 2026. Neither side defines how a vulnerability found on one reaches the other's risk process. We contribute a four-question classification procedure, a five-regime traceability matrix, a reference architecture with four handoff paths and three boundary findings. On 75 classified products from a frozen public-source corpus, the procedure yields 47 Periphery, 11 Core, 1 Other and 16 Boundary products, three

translated_title: 软件定义汽车的跨边界漏洞管理：ISO/SAE 21434与欧盟《网络弹性法案》接口处的可追溯性架构
translated_abstract: 软件定义汽车依赖于处于不同欧盟法规体系之下的产品。通过型式认证的车辆及其配套的系统、组件和独立技术单元受欧盟法规(EU) 2019/2144管辖，该法规使UN R155成为强制性要求；法规(EU) 2018/858对R156作出了同样规定；ISO/SAE 21434则支持R155所要求的管理体系。而充电器、配套应用程序、售后改装设备及许多后端系统可能转而属于《网络弹性法案》（CRA）的管辖范围，该法案第14条规定的报告义务自2026年9月11日起已开始适用。然而，双方均未定义在一方发现的漏洞如何传递到另一方的风险处理流程中。本文的贡献包括：一个四问题分类程序、一个覆盖五类法规体系的可追溯性矩阵、一个包含四条移交路径的参考架构，以及三项边界发现。基于一个冻结的公开来源语料库，对75个已分类产品的分析得出47个外围产品、11个核心产品、1个其他产品和16个边界产品……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 针对软件定义汽车中车辆型式认证法规体系（ISO/SAE 21434、UN R155/R156）与欧盟《网络弹性法案》之间漏洞管理交接的空白，提出了四问题分类程序、五法规体系可追溯性矩阵和含四条移交路径的参考架构，实现跨法规边界的漏洞可追溯管理。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a four-question classification procedure, a five-regime traceability matrix, and a reference architecture with four handoff paths to bridge the vulnerability management gap at the interface between vehicle type-approval regulations (ISO/SAE 21434, UN R155/R156) and the EU Cyber Resilience Act for software-defined vehicles.
